- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.2) mid-period, adjust forecast downward by 3–5% from peak to reflect risk-off behavior.
- Model tends to overestimate early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — apply a 2–3% downward bias for days 1–7.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), forecast should taper off by 1–2% per subsequent day to reflect mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows repeated high positive values followed by low values, model overestimates later days — apply a 3–5% downward correction for days 15–30.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) across 3–5 days, model tends to underestimate — add 2–4% to forecast for days 1–5 to compensate for subdued market sentiment.
